title: Creamy Chilli Tofu
style: Crisp tofu in a silky chilli-garlic sauce that gets its creaminess from blended silken tofu instead of coconut milk — big flavour, light on calories
description: Air-fried tofu in a creamy chilli-garlic sauce built on blended silken tofu — about 365 kcal and 34 g protein per serving, with none of the coconut milk or cream.

items.note: pressed 15 min, cut into 2 cm cubes
or a quick spray if air-frying

items.item: chilli oil or crispy chilli flakes

steps: Coat the tofu: Toss the cubes with soy sauce first, then cornstarch and garlic powder, so the starch sticks in a thin even layer.

Crisp it: Air-fry at 200°C / 400°F for 15–18 minutes, shaking twice, until golden and firm. Or dry-fry in a non-stick pan with 1 tsp oil over medium-high, 10–12 minutes, leaving each side undisturbed to form a crust.
Sauce: Blend the silken tofu, sambal, soy sauce, rice vinegar, garlic, maple syrup, and sesame oil until completely smooth. Add water a tablespoon at a time until it pours like double cream.
Warm it through: Pour the sauce into a small pan over low heat and warm gently for 2–3 minutes, stirring. Keep it low — silken tofu splits if you boil it hard.
Taste and adjust: more sambal for heat, vinegar for sharpness, a pinch of salt if it reads flat.
Spoon the warm sauce over the crisp tofu, or pool it underneath so the tofu stays crunchy. Finish with spring onions and sesame seeds.
tips: Blended silken tofu is the whole trick — you get the mouthfeel of a cream sauce for roughly a tenth of the fat.
Never let the sauce boil. Low and slow keeps it glossy instead of grainy.
Sauce under the tofu, not over it, if you care about the crunch surviving to the table.
The sauce is also excellent cold as a dip or a noodle-salad dressing — it thickens in the fridge, so loosen with water.
To push protein higher without the calories, serve over edamame and greens instead of rice.
